summary: Accept actions/checkout and actions/upload-artifact in the demo template: first-party, MIT, no advisories, SHA-pinned; pins moved from v4 (node20) to the current v7.0.1
basis: Evaluated the only third-party components #22 adds, the two Actions in templates/github/workflows/ballast-demo.yml, against docs/policies/dependencies.md and its project file. demo.py and the other tools import only the standard library; no manifest or lockfile changed. Both actions are GitHub-maintained, MIT, active, with no GitHub advisory, and are pinned by full commit SHA verified with git ls-remote. The implemented pins were v4.2.2 and v4.6.2 (node20, three majors behind) although tasks.md asks for the current release tag; this review moved both to the v7.0.1 SHAs after checking the v5-v7 release notes and the v7.0.1 action.yml inputs (unchanged for this template), and tests/test_demo.py passes. The template keeps persist-credentials false and a single-file upload path, which rules out the token-in-artifact risk class. Residual: Ballast's Dependabot does not scan templates/github/workflows, so the shipped pins can drift again. Same-provider review.

findings.label: implementation-bug
findings.reason: The template pinned actions/checkout v4.2.2 and actions/upload-artifact v4.6.2 (node20, three majors behind) although tasks.md requires the current release tag and ci.yml already uses checkout v7.0.1. Both are now pinned to the v7.0.1 commit SHAs; inputs are unchanged and tests/test_demo.py passes.

findings.label: architecture-issue
findings.reason: Dependabot scans only .github/workflows, so the shipped templates/github/workflows/ballast-demo.yml pins never get update PRs. Add the template directory to Ballast's own Dependabot config or a release-time check that template pins match their current release.
